title: Fire Emblem: Path of Radiance
subtitle: A mercenary takes command
summary: Fire Emblem: Path of Radiance brings the tactical role-playing series to GameCube and introduces Ike, a young mercenary on the continent of Tellius. body: Fire Emblem: Path of Radiance brings the tactical role-playing series to GameCube and introduces Ike, a young mercenary on the continent of Tellius. After Daein invades Crimea, his company becomes involved in Princess Elincia’s attempt to reclaim her kingdom. The journey crosses a world divided between the human beorc and the transforming laguz. Its political conflict gives the battles a context beyond advancing an army across a map, while Ike’s position outside the nobility supplies a different starting point for the adventure.

Battles unfold on a grid, with each unit’s movement, weapon and role shaping its useful position. Sending a fighter forward can open a route and expose that fighter to several enemies at once. Experience makes survivors stronger, so protecting a familiar unit also protects the time invested in it. Permanent losses give mistakes a lasting consequence. The tactical question is therefore rarely just whether an enemy can be defeated this turn; it is whether the resulting arrangement leaves the company able to survive the next one.

Path of Radiance was the series’ first fully three-dimensional entry, returning Fire Emblem to a home console after its Game Boy Advance games. The larger presentation serves a campaign still built around individual units and their place in a growing company. Tellius also gives the series a setting it can revisit: Radiant Dawn later continues its history on Wii. Here, the contrast between peoples and social positions remains central to the journey, linking the movement of armies with the people affected by the war.
